text:
maya: Heads-up: prepping a Private deployment for Acme that needs sealed-compute guarantees + HSM attestation. Looking for a compact checklist for VPC/on-prem network hardening, RBAC deltas, audit logging and KMS integration. Any gotchas? :lock:

aditya: we did something similar last quarter. TL;DR: 1) deny-all egress default 2) explicit egress to KMS HSM endpoints 3) mTLS between service SA and keystore + attestation via TPM/HSM.

cheng: +1 to deny-all. If you can run Cilium, use CiliumNetworkPolicy L7 to prevent accidental plaintext egress. eBPF makes l7 enforcement much cheaper than iptables. :rocket:

riley: audit question — retention and tamper-resistance? customer requires 1y retention and signed append-only logs. we used fluent-bit -> syslog-ng -> onprem SIEM with gzip+sha256 manifests. also enable Kubernetes audit policy at the apiserver for write/exec events.

sam: RBAC notes: create narrow service account roles for any process that touches keys. example pattern: kms-decrypt-only, kms-sign-only, and a separate bootstrap role scoped to the attestation workflow. avoid giving pods the node-level creds.

maya: any sample NetworkPolicy we can ship to the infra repo? keep it minimal for review.

aditya: here's a tiny starting point for k8s NetPol (deny all egress except KMS and internal services):
```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-egress-except-kms
  namespace: ml-serving
spec:
  podSelector: {} # apply to all pods in namespace
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.10.20.0/24 # internal infra
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 192.0.2.10/32 # KMS HSM endpoint (example)
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 443
```
Note: replace IP with private link or NATed IP provided by customer.

cheng: if using Cilium, you can do L7 rules instead of IP cidr so you don't need stable IPs (e.g., allow DNS service name or KMS FQDN). Also recommend egress policy for DNS+time-sync only.

ops-jen: for onprem deploys we added a host-level egress proxy enforced via iptables on jump hosts so we can audit initial bootstrap. Works well for air-gapped customers who allow explicit outbound.

riley: audit logging extras: - sign audit batches with fleet key - forward to immutable storage (WORM) - log key use events from KMS (Encrypt/Decrypt/Sign) with correlation id to request.

sam: RBAC practical: provide example kubectl to create decrypt-only role:
```bash
kubectl create role kms-decrypt --verb=get --resource=secrets --namespace=ml-serving
# bind to serviceaccount
kubectl create rolebinding rb-kms-decrypt --role=kms-decrypt --serviceaccount=ml-serving:inference-sa --namespace=ml-serving
```
Then attach annotation with key-id and audit label.

maya: Incident scenario: if a key is suspected compromised, what's the step sequence? rotate? revoke? fallback?

security-oncall: Runbook (short): 1) Quarantine affected workload (apply network deny-all to its podSelector) 2) Revoke current key (HSM revoke) 3) Issue rotated key + update KMS bindings 4) Re-issue ephemeral bootstrap creds for services and rotate service tokens 5) Reingest audit logs for scope and scope CVEs 6) post-mortem + customer notification if needed. See internal runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kms-incident (private). :warning:

ops-jen: one addition — if HSM supports key wrapping, pre-provision a wrapping key so you can rewrap data instead of decrypt/reencrypt heavy flows during rotation. saved us hours during an earlier rotation.

aditya: watch out for clock skew; attestation tokens are TTL-based. If customers have NTP drift, attestation fails and the cluster hits a hard-degraded state. Add monitoring on attestor failures.

maya: awesome. I'll assemble PR for infra repo with NetPol + RBAC templates and a short incident appendix. tagging @cheng to review Cilium rules and @security-oncall to vet runbook appendix. Thanks all :heart:
